## Summary

Replaces PR #145's fixed `scale(1.10)` with a **per-image adaptive crop** computed from the detector's measured border depth + the live wrapper/source dimensions. Closes the residual-white-band gap Maya identified in the post-#145 production audit: 401 WEST #6 still had 20 px white visible per edge after scale(1.10); this PR drives that to ≤ 5 px.

## What changes

### `lib/media/white-border-detector.ts`
- **`BorderDetectionResult` extended** to include `depthRatios: { top, bottom, left, right }` — per-edge contiguous-white depth as a fraction of the source dimension. Always populated (even on `hasBorder=false`) so callers can inspect.
- **New `computeAdaptiveCropScale()`** — the math. Cover-aware: accounts for the L/R or T/B border that `object-fit: cover` already absorbs before any extra scale is applied. Clamped to `[1, 1.5]`. Fully documented + unit-tested.
- **New thresholds**: `depthWhiteRatioThreshold = 0.85` (depth-walk row/column whiteness), `adaptiveScaleClampMax = 1.5` (hard ceiling).
- **`detectWhiteBorder(img)` now returns** the structured `BorderDetectionResult` instead of bare `boolean`.

### `app/components/IDXImage.tsx`
- State shape `borderedSrc: string | null` → `borderedState: { src; scale } | null`. Atomic invalidation on src change preserved.
- `handleLoad` calls `computeAdaptiveCropScale` with the live wrapper rect + image natural dims, floors at `WHITE_BORDER_MIN_CROP_SCALE` (1.05), stores result in state.
- Render: `transform: hasWhiteBorder ? \`scale(\${cropScale})\` : undefined` — per-image scale instead of constant.
- Old `WHITE_BORDER_CROP_SCALE = 1.1` constant removed.
- Conditional `crossOrigin="anonymous"` on `autoCropWhiteBorder` **preserved unchanged**.
- liquidMotion animation still disabled **only** when `hasWhiteBorder`.
- `autoCropWhiteBorder` still default `false`; FeaturedListings still NOT opted in.

### `tests/runtime/white-border-detector.test.ts`
- All 18 existing tests preserved (false-positive guards intact).
- +5 tests for `depthRatios` accuracy (letterbox, 4-sided, clean control, type safety).
- +5 tests for `computeAdaptiveCropScale` math (no-border, degenerate inputs, clamp, L/R cover-absorption, heavy 4-sided, portrait-source symmetry).
- Source-pin updates for the new `borderedState` shape + adaptive render path.
- Total: **34 / 34 PASS**.

### `tests/e2e/search-card-after-proof.spec.ts`
- New "adaptive crop reduces visible white band ≤ 5 px" test in the existing describe block.
- Walks inward from each edge of the rendered image, captures the depth where row/column whiteness drops below 85%.
- **Hard assertions:**
  - 401 WEST #6 each edge depth ≤ 5 px
  - 401 WEST PH each edge depth ≤ 5 px
  - 15 W 68TH each edge depth = 0 (strict — no false positive)
- Existing FeaturedListings opt-out test (item 9) + desktop scale-applied test untouched.

|------|------------:|-------------:|---------------:|
| 401 WEST #6 | 20 px white per edge | ≤ 5 px (target) | ≈ 1.31× |
| 401 WEST PH | 18 px L/R | ≤ 5 px (target) | ≈ 1.07× |
| 15 W 68TH | 0 px clean | 0 px clean | 1.0× (no scale) |

Live Playwright proof will run against the PR preview / production after deploy.

| `npx eslint <changed>` | ✓ clean |
| `npx jest white-border-detector.test.ts` | ✓ **34 / 34 PASS** |
| `npm run compliance-check` | ✓ **93 / 93 BLOCKER+STRICT** |

author: mochengqian
body:
## Summary

Migrates the cluster runtime endpoint view from mutable `Config.Endpoints` +
`Endpoint.UnHealthy` into an immutable `EndpointSnapshot` published via
`atomic.Pointer`. Request-path picks read snapshots; health updates and
membership changes go through CAS replacement instead of mutating shared
state.
## Architecture

- `Cluster.endpoints atomic.Pointer[EndpointSnapshot]` publishes the
  immutable view. Health updates produce a new snapshot via CAS.
- `EndpointSnapshot` indexes endpoints by ID, address, and health, all
  precomputed at publish time so the request path is O(1) on the healthy
  view instead of an O(N) scan over `ClusterConfig.Endpoints`.
- `PickContext` carries snapshot + config into load balancers. Bundled
  balancers (round-robin, rand, weight-random, ring-hash, maglev)
  implement `SnapshotLoadBalancer`; legacy balancers keep working via
  the compatibility adapter, which serializes them through a
  package-level lock.
- `healthcheck.HealthChecker` emits `EndpointHealthEvent` via callback;
  the legacy direct-mutation path (`CreateHealthCheck` without a
  callback) is preserved for existing callers.
- LLM proxy cooldown state moved out of `Endpoint.Metadata` into a
  process-wide bounded store (`maxCooldownStoreEntries = 1024`) with a
  throttled sweep.

## Operator-visible behavior changes

(For the maintainer writing release notes — these belong in the
next CHANGELOG entry.)

- **Endpoint state is immutable post-publish.** Direct mutation of
  `Endpoint.UnHealthy` or `Endpoint.Metadata` after cluster start is no
  longer observed by the request path. Health updates go through
  `Cluster.UpdateEndpointHealth` / health-check callbacks; membership
  changes go through `Cluster.RefreshEndpoints`.
- **`Endpoint.UnHealthy` post-init mutation is no longer observed by the
  request path.** Code that flips `endpoint.UnHealthy = true/false` after
  the cluster has started will see no effect on which endpoints get picked;
  the snapshot is built once and only updated via
  `Cluster.UpdateEndpointHealth` (or via the health-check callback).
  Upgrade impact: any external integration that flipped this field
  directly will silently stop functioning. The healthcheck legacy path
  (`CreateHealthCheck` without callback) still mutates the field for
  backward compatibility, but pickers do not read it.
- **LLM proxy cooldown** moved out of `Endpoint.Metadata` into a
  bounded process-wide store. Constants `LLMUnhealthyKey` and
  `HealthyCheckTimeKey` are no longer written by the filter and are
  marked deprecated in source; suggest removal in v1.3.
- **Endpoint ID dedup** changed from "warn but allow collision" to
  "first wins, second gets a `-2` suffix". Operator-supplied colliding
  IDs become `<id>-2` (not `generated-<hash>-2`) so dashboards stay
  readable.
- **Health-check thresholds now actually take effect.** The
  `HealthyThreshold` / `UnhealthyThreshold` config values used to be
  compared against an uninitialized counter that was always zero, so
  any deployment's first probe flipped state regardless of config; on
  the non-timeout failure path there was no counter at all. Defaults
  remain 5/5. Deployments that depended on fire-on-first-probe should
  set both thresholds to `1` explicitly. Mixed timeout + negative
  responses now share one counter, so the threshold applies to total
  consecutive failures.

- **Endpoint ID is a trust boundary in the snapshot pick path.** When a
  snapshot endpoint's address is a blank-domain placeholder
  (`Domains == [""]`, `Address == ""`, `Port == 0`),
  `sameEndpointIdentity` accepts any balancer-returned address as long as
  the endpoint ID matches. This is a narrow wildcard for legacy resolvers
  that publish placeholder endpoints to be resolved downstream. Operators
  must treat endpoint IDs as system-controlled values; do not let untrusted
  input populate `endpoint.id` on a placeholder endpoint, because the ID
  alone is sufficient to match any picked address through that placeholder.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`
- [x] `go test ./...` — the only failure is
      `pkg/cluster/healthcheck/TestCheckTcpConn/failed_connection_due_to_invalid_address_format`,
      which fails on the base branch too (pre-existing, unrelated).
- [x] `go test -race ./pkg/cluster/... ./pkg/server/ ./pkg/cluster/loadbalancer/...
      ./pkg/filter/llm/proxy/ ./pkg/adapter/llmregistry/registry/nacos/
      ./pkg/model/`
- [x] `go test -race -count=20 -run TestClusterRefreshAndHealthUpdateConcurrent
      ./pkg/cluster/` — locks the snapshot CAS invariant under concurrent
      `RefreshEndpoints` + `UpdateEndpointHealth` writers.
- [x] `go test -bench=. -benchmem -count=3 ./pkg/server/` — numbers below.
- [x] `go mod tidy && git diff --quiet go.mod go.sum`
- [x] Optional pre-merge soak (PR author or release owner):
      deploy a race-detector build to staging after code review approval;
      observe `pixiu_request_elapsed` p99 drift < 20% and zero `DATA RACE` /
      `panic:` over 24h. Not required for local review; run only if staging
      capacity is available.

## Benchmark (Apple M5)

Request-path endpoint retrieval on the snapshot pick path
(`HealthyEndpointsForPick`, which the actual request handler uses):

```
endpoints=8    healthy=100%   0.46 ns/op   0 B/op   0 allocs/op
endpoints=64   healthy=100%   0.46 ns/op   0 B/op   0 allocs/op
endpoints=512  healthy=100%   0.46 ns/op   0 B/op   0 allocs/op
```

For comparison, the defensive `HealthyEndpoints()` accessor (used by
external callers that need an isolated slice — not the request path):

```
endpoints=8    healthy=100%      279 ns/op    1216 B/op    9 allocs/op
endpoints=64   healthy=100%     2157 ns/op    9728 B/op   65 allocs/op
endpoints=512  healthy=100%    17099 ns/op   78592 B/op  513 allocs/op
```

End-to-end pick (`PickEndpoint` through round-robin):

```
clusters=1     RoundRobin     130 ns/op    144 B/op   1 allocs/op
clusters=1024  RoundRobin     147 ns/op    144 B/op   1 allocs/op
```

## Known follow-ups (separate issues, all filed before merge)

- #938 — collapse `EndpointChecker.HandleFailure(timeout bool)` in the next major release.
- #939 — drop `sharedCooldownStore` global and inject cooldownStore via `ClusterManager`.
- #940 — avoid double-cloning endpoints across the assemble/publish boundary.
- #941 — move `ZeroCopy` / `HealthyOnly` snapshot marker interfaces behind an internal boundary.
- #942 — cache consistent hash when the healthy endpoint set is unchanged.
- #943 — replace O(N) cooldown LRU eviction with `container/list`.
- #944 — add snapshot publish and endpoint count metrics.
- #945 — enable staticcheck SA1019 for deprecated symbol usage.
- #949 — RFC: treat duplicate endpoint IDs as a hard configuration error
  (raised in https://github.com/apache/dubbo-go-pixiu/pull/932#issuecomment-4566120689)
- #950 — chore: audit "unified static/dynamic" helpers in pkg/server/cluster_manager.go

## Reviewer-raised items intentionally kept

- **`EndpointSnapshot` nil-receiver guards on accessor methods** — kept for a consistent nil-safe accessor surface.
- **Public `Cluster.Config`** — making it private is intentionally out of scope; it touches many callsites and belongs in the later decoupling series.
- **`compareAndSetStore` Version equality** — pre-existing behavior, not introduced by this PR.
- **`assembleClusterEndpoints` plus snapshot double-clone** — tracked in #940 so clone-boundary semantics can be reviewed separately from the snapshot mechanism.

## Out of scope (tracked as tech debt)
- `Cluster.Config` remains public in this PR. Making it private + adding
  getters touches ~20 callsites and belongs in the decoupling series after
  PR-3 lands; target: decoupling PR-6, together with runtime ownership cleanup.
- `LLMUnhealthyKey` / `HealthyCheckTimeKey` are deprecated here for downstream
  compatibility. Target removal: v1.3 cleanup PR, after one minor-release
  migration window.

## Description

Replaces the theseus-based multi-segment MSA with abPOA's subgraph alignment API. Each read segment is aligned only against the relevant portion of the graph between two boundary nodes, rather than the full graph.

**Approach:**
1. Backbone added as first sequence, creating a linear POA graph (one node per base)
2. Boundary node IDs precomputed at each segment junction
3. `abpoa_align_sequence_to_subgraph` + `abpoa_add_subgraph_alignment` used per read segment

**Results on test fastq:** 52 reads, 1402 segments aligned in 7.6s (5.4ms/seg avg). Three segments spanning >100 backbone boundaries take 0.1–1s each (structurally large subgraph alignments).

## How to test

```bash
cd build && make -j
./dinara --input ../tests/GIAB_HG002_PAW70337_RAW_chr1_15-15.4.fastq \
  --Reads.minReadLength 1000 --threads 4 --Kmers.k 50 \
  --Kmers.useSimdClosedSyncmers true --Kmers.syncmerS 11 \
  --Assembly.mode3.minAnchorCoverage 4 --Assembly.mode3.maxAnchorCoverage 400 \
  --Align.minAlignedMarkerCount 2 --Align.minAlignedFraction 0 \
  --OverlapCandidates.method InvertedIndex \
  --OverlapCandidates.driftRateTolerance 0.05 \
  --OverlapCandidates.maxEndFuzz 0 --OverlapCandidates.minOverlapLength 0 \
  --memoryMode anonymous --memoryBacking 4K
```

body:
## Issue

This PR adds a count limit to the message delivery records kept by peer scoring.

Peer scoring keeps a short-lived delivery record for each message ID it is tracking. These records are used while a message moves through validation, and they help account for duplicate deliveries, near-first deliveries, valid messages, invalid messages, ignored messages, and throttled validation. Today those records expire after `SeenMsgTTL`, but there is no count-based limit on how many can exist during that TTL window.

That means memory use can grow with the rate of unique messages that reach validation or delivery tracing. This is not a permanent leak, because the records are eventually removed by delivery-record GC. The issue is the active window: on a busy topic, or under adversarial traffic, peers can keep sending unique messages and cause the delivery-record map to grow until those records age out.

For production nodes with peer scoring enabled, this creates a resource-scaling problem. Memory use is bounded by time, but not by volume. A high enough message rate during `SeenMsgTTL` can still create a large number of retained records.

## Fix

This change adds a configurable cap for peer score delivery records.

`PeerScoreParams` now has a `DeliveryRecordCap` field. If it is left as zero, peer scoring uses `DefaultDeliveryRecordCap`. When the delivery-record table reaches the cap, `getRecord` first runs GC to clear any expired records. If the table is still full after that, it does not allocate a new tracking record for the new message ID.

Existing tracked records continue to work as before. The fix also keeps direct scoring behavior where possible: first-message delivery scoring still runs before delivery-record tracking, and validation-failed messages still penalize the sender even when the record table is full. What gets skipped at capacity is the extra per-message tracking used for duplicate and near-first delivery accounting.

This keeps memory bounded without adding new goroutines, changing message delivery behavior, or blocking the validation path. Operators that expect very high message throughput can raise the cap through score params.

## Tests

This PR adds coverage at both the score layer and the GossipSub layer.

`TestScoreDeliveryRecordCap` checks the delivery-record table directly. It verifies that the table does not grow beyond the configured cap, that invalid-message scoring still applies when the cap is full, and that new records can be created again after old records expire and GC runs.

`TestGossipsubScoreDeliveryRecordCap` drives the same behavior through real GossipSub publish and subscribe flow with peer scoring enabled. It publishes more unique messages than the configured cap, verifies those messages are still delivered, and checks that the peer score delivery-record table remains capped.

The peer score parameter validation tests were also updated so negative caps are rejected and valid configured caps are accepted.

Closes #6

## Summary

Adds the first CI pipeline for `noorinalabs-isnad-ingest-platform`. Until this lands, **all Python code in this repo has merged without any automated checks** — 59 source files, 20+ test files, zero CI. This is the Tier-1 unblocker for the rest of P3W11 in this repo; every other W11 PR has been merging blind.

## Workflow shape (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)

Triggers: `pull_request` against `main` and `deployments/**`, plus `push` to `main`. Cancel-in-progress concurrency keyed by ref.

| Job | Steps |
|---|---|
| `lint-and-typecheck` | `uv sync` → `ruff check src/ workers/ tests/` → `ruff format --check src/ workers/ tests/` → `mypy src/` |
| `security-audit` | `uv sync` → `uv export --no-hashes --frozen --no-emit-project > /tmp/requirements.txt` → `pip-audit --strict --desc -r /tmp/requirements.txt` |
| `test` | `uv sync` → `pytest tests/ -v --tb=short -m "not integration"` with `ENVIRONMENT=test` |

Notes:
- Lint/format scope is `src/ workers/ tests/` to match `Makefile` `lint`/`format` targets — `workers/` is a sibling top-level package in this repo (unlike `noorinalabs-isnad-graph`)
- `ruff format --check` (NOT `ruff format`) — read-only gate, never auto-fixes
- Integration tests excluded via `-m "not integration"` — the `integration` marker is registered in `pyproject.toml:122`
- `uv` install via `astral-sh/setup-uv@v7` with `uv.lock`-keyed cache (lift from sister-repo CI)
- Workflow uses Python 3.14 implicitly via `uv sync` + `requires-python = ">=3.14"` in `pyproject.toml` — no separate `actions/setup-python` step needed
- Modeled on `noorinalabs-isnad-graph/.github/workflows/ci.yml` (issue body said `noorinalabs-isnad-graph-ingestion` — STALE, the repo is `noorinalabs-isnad-graph`)

## Pre-existing failure #1 surfaced + handled inline (mypy)

Running `mypy --strict` against current HEAD surfaced 4 pre-existing errors in `src/cli.py:447-453`:

```
src/cli.py:448: error: Argument "object_store" to "PipelineResetter" has incompatible type "object"; expected "_ObjectStoreProto"  [arg-type]
src/cli.py:449: error: Argument "kafka_admin" to "PipelineResetter" has incompatible type "object"; expected "KafkaAdmin"  [arg-type]
src/cli.py:450: error: Argument "neo4j" to "PipelineResetter" has incompatible type "object"; expected "Neo4jResetter"  [arg-type]
src/cli.py:451: error: Argument "pg" to "PipelineResetter" has incompatible type "object"; expected "PgResetter"  [arg-type]
```

Root cause: `_build_reset_clients` deliberately returns `tuple[object, ...]` to keep heavy SDK imports (`kafka`/`neo4j`/`boto3`) inside the function body so unit tests can monkey-patch adapters without paying the import cost. Tuple type-erasure was the workaround; the call-site type contract is the cost.

**Applied inline** (this PR): `# type: ignore[arg-type]` per call site, four lines. Minimum needed to satisfy the new gate.

**Filed as follow-up**: noorinalabs/noorinalabs-isnad-ingest-platform#31 — narrow `_build_reset_clients` to the proper protocol contract (or expose four typed factory helpers) and remove the four type-ignore comments.

This split — minimal in-PR fix to unblock the gate + proper-fix issue tracked separately — is per the spawn brief's multi-layer-gap discipline.

## Pre-existing failure #2 surfaced + handled inline (pip-audit, after reviewer feedback)

First-strict-`pip-audit` run reported 6 CVEs across 4 dependency packages. Per reviewer guidance, these are different shape from arbitrary fixes — patch-version bumps, no API risk, and merging without them would land main red on the very gate this PR introduces. Bundled in second commit (`0823c9e`):

| Package | Before | After | CVEs cleared |
|---|---|---|---|
| `urllib3` | 2.6.3 | 2.7.0 | CVE-2026-44431 (cross-origin header leak), CVE-2026-44432 (Brotli streaming decompression) |
| `lxml` | 6.0.2 | 6.1.0 | CVE-2026-41066 (default `resolve_entities` change) |
| `pip` | 26.0.1 | 26.1.1 | CVE-2026-3219 (tar/ZIP archive confusion), CVE-2026-6357 (self-update import ordering) |
| `pytest` | 9.0.2 | 9.0.3 | CVE-2025-71176 (`/tmp/pytest-of-{user}` privilege escalation) |

Local `pip-audit --strict` now reports **"No known vulnerabilities found"**. Full pytest suite (544 passed, 4 skipped, 13 deselected) still green; lint, format, mypy unchanged.

CVE-2026-3219 had no `Fix Versions` listed in the audit DB at first-run time but pip 26.1.1 (a forward-bump beyond the 26.1 fix for CVE-2026-6357) clears it as well — no `--ignore-vuln` needed.

**Retro candidate**: when a first-time `pip-audit --strict` lands on a repo without prior CI, expect to bundle pre-existing CVE bumps in the same PR by default. Different shape from arbitrary type/lint debt — see multi-layer-gap discipline carve-out.

## Live trace (post-push CI run)

First run (pre-dep-bump, 2/3 green): https://github.com/noorinalabs/noorinalabs-isnad-ingest-platform/actions/runs/25980907307 — `lint-and-typecheck` ✓, `test` ✓, `security-audit` ✗ (the 6 CVEs above).

Second run (post-dep-bump on commit `0823c9e`) — verifying as of this body update; will be linked in a PR comment once it settles.

## Tech Debt

None introduced. The new CI workflow gates future PRs against existing Makefile targets; no new debt is created by adding the gate itself. Any pre-existing failures surfaced will be tracked as separate follow-up issues.

## Reviewers

- **Primary**: @bjorn-henriksen (Bjørn Henriksen, DevOps Architect — ingest-platform owner)
- **Secondary**: @aino-virtanen (Aino Virtanen, Standards & Quality Lead, parent org — CI gates are org-wide charter territory)

Fixes #718, #719, #720 — three related auth/setup defects in one PR.

## Summary

### #718 — Token refresh failure left UI authenticated
\`refreshToken()\` in \`useAuth.ts\` kept \`isAuthenticated=true\` and the last access token when \`/api/auth/refresh\` failed. The UI and WebSocket continued operating with stale credentials → repeated 401s and a false authenticated state. Both the \`!response.ok\` branch and the catch branch now drop auth state and CSRF token before returning null.

### #719 — Setup wizard completed when auto-login failed
\`SetupWizard.handleSubmit()\` called \`onComplete()\` even when the post-setup auto-login returned false, dropping the user into the main UI unauthenticated. The wizard now stays open and surfaces the error.

### #720 — SSO providers contract mismatch
Backend returns \`{ providers: string[] }\`. UI typed it as \`{ name, enabled }[]\` and read \`.name\` / \`.enabled\` — both undefined on a string. \`hasEnabledSso\` was permanently false, the SSO section never rendered (Microsoft "missing"), and any direct hit at \`/sso/login\` fell through to \`GetProvider\`'s "Invalid provider" error. UI now uses the string list directly; \`initOAuthManager\` already filters to providers that are Enabled AND have a ClientID, so presence in the list is sufficient.

- [x] \`npx vite build\` succeeds

- **New `kul-loader` crate.** Given a project-root path, returns `LoadedProject { manifest_name, manifest_yaml, inputs }` or a typed `ProjectLoadError` (`ManifestNotFound`, `ManifestReadFailed`, `DirectoryReadFailed`, `InputReadFailed`). Encapsulates `kul.yml` discovery, `*.kul` enumeration (flat-directory per ADR-0015), and IO error variants. Lives outside `kul-core` (which forbids filesystem IO) and outside `kul-cli` (which already depends on `kul-lsp` — placing the loader inside `kul-cli` would put it out of `kul-lsp`'s reach in slice 5).
- **CWD-rooted CLI subcommands.** `kul validate`, `kul format`, `kul export` lose their positional `<FILE>` argument. Each discovers the project from CWD, calls `kul_core::check` once, and renders:
  - `validate`: diagnostics for every `.kul` file in one pass, single `ok` on success.
  - `format`: rewrites every `.kul` file in place (or, with `--check`, lists not-formatted files without writing).
  - `export`: one envelope unioning every file's persons, marriages, and parenthood links.
- **Clear non-project-root error.** Each subcommand prints `not a Kul project root: no kul.yml in current directory` and exits 1 when CWD has no manifest. The CLI-side `commands::manifest` helper is gone — `KUL-M01` discovery is now the loader's job.
- **Tests.** 9 loader unit tests (snapshot-locked error rendering); 20 CLI integration tests covering both single-file and multi-file projects, the `examples/07-multi-file-extended-family/` smoke, and deliberately-broken fixtures that surface cross-file R01 / R02 / R13.
- **Architecture doc updated.** Pipeline narrative reflects CLI now feeding `N>=1` `.kul` inputs per `check`; crate map and dependency graph gain `kul-loader`.

`kul lsp`, the WASM bridge, and `kul_core::check` itself are unchanged in this slice. The LSP multi-file lift lands as #85.

author: michaelchar
body:
## Summary

Sign-in for students and landlords sat with a frozen "Submitting…" button for several seconds. Diagnosis traced the wait to a chain of avoidable Supabase Auth round-trips: a defensive `signOut()` before every login, plus `getUserFromToken` (which hits `supabase.auth.getUser` over HTTP) being called from `/api/auth/session`, every `requireStudent`/`requireLandlord` RSC check, and every authenticated API route — including the four parallel ones the landlord dashboard fires on mount. Cloudflare Worker cold starts compound everything.

Three commits in rollout order:

- **8ac6426** — Skip pre-login `signOut()` when no session exists (saves ~200–1000 ms per login on the common fresh-login path), add a `/api/health` warmup ping on login-page mount to hide Worker cold-start latency, and replace the frozen "Signing in…" string with a two-stage label (Authenticating → Loading your account/dashboard).
- **ed2adb7** — Verify Supabase JWTs locally with `jose` (HS256 with `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET`) instead of calling `supabase.auth.getUser`. This is the biggest win: it removes a ~200–1000 ms Supabase round-trip from every authenticated server check. Fallback path preserved for when the secret isn't set, so the change doesn't dark-launch in prod until the secret is propagated. Audience pinned to `"authenticated"`. 7 new unit tests.
- **761a914** — Wrap the `/student/account` inquiry list in `<Suspense>` so the page shell (heading, "signed in as", sign-out button) paints on the first byte and the rows stream in.

Net effect on the student post-login critical path: roughly halves the user-visible wait on warm paths and removes the biggest cold-path tail.

## ⚠️ Prerequisite before merge

Commit `ed2adb7` needs `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` set as a Worker secret in prod before it can take its speedup path:

```bash
wrangler secret put SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET --name studentx
```

Value comes from Supabase Dashboard → Project Settings → API → JWT Settings → JWT Secret.

If the secret isn't set, `getUserFromToken` falls back to the original network call — behaviour stays identical, just no speedup. So merging without setting the secret is safe; setting it after merge is what flips on the win.

## Discovered during rebase

The recent PR #170/#171 added a `/api/student/profile` POST inside the student login flow (idempotent profile probe). That route also calls `getUserFromToken`, so commit `ed2adb7` speeds it up too without further code changes.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run lint` — clean (one pre-existing unrelated warning in cf/worker-entry.mjs)
- [x] `npm run test` — 131 tests pass, including 7 new tests for `verifyAccessTokenLocal`
- [x] `npm run build` — succeeds, `/api/health` route registered
- [ ] After deploy: log in as a test student, time click → rendered account page, confirm under ~1.5 s on a warm Worker
- [ ] After deploy: same with a test landlord; confirm dashboard skeleton appears immediately, content settles quickly
- [ ] Watch the `landlord-listings-api` synthetic canary (`/api/cron/synthetic-en-listing`) for 15 minutes post-deploy — it exercises `requireLandlord`, so if local JWT verification breaks the check goes red
- [ ] Cold-path: wait 10+ min for the Worker isolate to evict, then sign in; confirm well under the 15 s timeout ceiling

body:
## Summary

Applies workflow security improvements proposed in the recent session audit. All 7 workflow files now have:

- **Explicit top-level \`permissions:\`** (either \`{}\` deny-all or \`contents: read\` per workflow) — independent of repo-level "Workflow permissions" setting (defense in depth).
- **Concurrency groups** to prevent parallel-run races, with \`cancel-in-progress\` set per workflow's safety requirements.
- **Fork guards** (\`if: github.repository == 'smorin/doxa-research'\`) on scheduled real-API workflows so forks don't burn API quota with our cron.

Plus a chore commit to whitelist a pre-existing gitleaks false-positive in RELEASE-PLEASE-APP.md (the doc example showing what a PEM private key looks like was matching gitleaks' private-key regex by structure).

See commit messages for full per-workflow details.

## Test plan

This PR exists primarily to TEST the workflow changes via the events they fire on:

| Phase | Verification |
|---|---|
| ✅ Phase 1 (pre-flight) | yamllint, actionlint, YAML parse, runtime commands all green locally |
| 🔄 Phase 2 (this PR) | ci.yml, codeql.yml, commitlint.yml run on the PR event |
| ⏳ Phase 3 (after merge) | ci.yml, codeql.yml, release-please.yml run on push-to-main |
| ⏳ Phase 4 (manual) | \`gh workflow run\` extended.yml and live-api.yml |
| ⏳ Phase 5a (security validation) | tag a non-main commit; new \`verify tag is on main\` check should fail it |
| ⏳ Phase 5b (real release) | merge the release-please Release PR; full publish.yml → PyPI |

## Risk

LOW. Local repo permissions setting is already "read" so the explicit \`permissions:\` declarations are documentation, not behavioral change. Concurrency adds determinism; nothing that worked before should fail. Fork guards close an attack surface that doesn't exist today but would matter if the repo gains forks.

Behavioral changes at runtime:
- Scheduled extended/live-api on a fork would skip the job (intended)
- Two simultaneous publish triggers on the same tag would serialize instead of race (intended)
- A force-pushed PR no longer keeps the prior commitlint run in-flight; the new run cancels the old (intended)

## Summary
- Pin every "what day is it / is class now?" decision to Asia/Taipei across the iOS app, the Watch app, and the Widget extension — NTUST's class table, ICS feed, and Moodle deadlines are all authored in Taipei wall time, so a student abroad would otherwise see the wrong weekday's courses and a wrong "ongoing" state.
- Repoint `DateFormatter`s that previously inherited the device TZ (including `SDCourse.isoFormatter` and the widget's `dateKey`, which must agree on `yyyy-MM-dd` for skip-state lookups to match).
- Add a `TimezoneObserver` (reactive to `NSSystemTimeZoneDidChange` + debug-clock flips); the iOS app shows the `app_non_taipei_timezone_hint` as a one-shot `.alert` whenever the app re-enters the foreground (fresh launch via `.onAppear`, multitask return via `scenePhase → .active`). - `swift/Shared/TaipeiCalendar.swift` — `SharedTaipei.{timeZone, calendar}` used by main app + watch (Shared/ is in both targets).
- `swift/TigerDuck/App/AppConstants.swift` — re-exports as `AppConstants.taipeiTimeZone` / `taipeiCalendar`.
- `swift/TigerDuckWidgets/Logic/WidgetTaipei.swift` — local duplicate inside the widget extension target (Shared/ isn't included there).

body:
## Problem

`TOR_NICKNAME`, `TOR_CONTACT`, `TOR_BANDWIDTH_RATE`, and `TOR_BANDWIDTH_BURST` were documented as ways to configure the relay, but were silently ignored at runtime. Tor reads `torrc` directly and has no native env var expansion — the variables never made it into the config.

## Fix

Added `entrypoint.sh` which:
1. Copies the read-only `/etc/tor/torrc` mount to `/tmp/torrc`
2. Applies `sed` substitutions for any env vars that are set
3. `exec`s `tor -f /tmp/torrc`

The `torrc` mount stays read-only. Unset env vars are skipped so the torrc placeholder/default values remain as fallback.

The pre-existing `test_cwd_hash_matches_shell_pwd_sha1sum` spot-checks the Python hash function against an in-test Python reimplementation — that's Python-vs-Python parity. It does NOT catch divergence between the librarian skill's actual shell pipeline (in SKILL.md step 0) and the Python `_cwd_sentinel_hash` implementation. 3. `test_skill_md_uses_expected_shell_pipeline` — parse SKILL.md and assert it still contains the canonical pipeline string. If the skill drifts, this test fails before the parity test even runs, so reviewers are pointed at the source of the drift (the skill, not the hook).

Ảnh sau khử nhiễu vẫn còn chấm/đường mảnh nhỏ làm bẩn input OCR. PR này thêm bước lọc sau `BitwiseNot` để giữ nét số và loại phần nhiễu diện tích nhỏ trước khi OCR và trước khi lưu ảnh `zzz`.

- **Pre-OCR noise cleanup (sau `BitwiseNot`)**
  - Thêm `MedianBlur` (kernel 3) để triệt pixel lẻ.
  - Thêm lọc contour theo diện tích để loại blob nhỏ (`minAreaRatio = 0.003`).

- **Helper mới trong image processing**
  - Bổ sung `RemoveSmallBlobs(Mat blackOnWhite, double minAreaRatio = 0.003)`.
  - Cách làm: invert ảnh, `FindContours` external, chỉ giữ contour có diện tích >= ngưỡng theo tỷ lệ diện tích ảnh.

- **Wiring vào pipeline OCR hiện có**
  - Dùng `cleaned` thay `forOcr` cho:
    - `TryFullImageOcr(...)`
    - `RecognizePerChar(...)`
    - Ảnh trả về để lưu vào thư mục `zzz`
  - Không thay đổi logic Tesseract/deskew/rotation.

- **Resource ownership / lifetime**
  - Dùng `using` cho các `Mat` tạm (`forOcr`, `medBlurred`, `cleaned`).
  - Trả về ảnh bằng `Clone()` để ownership rõ ràng cho caller.

```csharp
using var forOcr = new Mat();
Cv2.BitwiseNot(scaled, forOcr);

using var medBlurred = new Mat();
Cv2.MedianBlur(forOcr, medBlurred, 3);

using var cleaned = RemoveSmallBlobs(medBlurred, minAreaRatio: 0.003);

string? fullResult = TryFullImageOcr(cleaned);
if (fullResult != null) return (fullResult, cleaned.Clone());
return (RecognizePerChar(cleaned, scaledW, scaledH), cleaned.Clone());
```

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Vấn đề

Ảnh sau khi khử nhiễu vẫn còn nhiều chi tiết thừa (chấm lẻ, đường kẻ mảnh, noise nhỏ), người dùng muốn chỉ giữ lại phần nét số, loại bỏ hoàn toàn các pixel nhiễu còn sót lại.

## Nguyên nhân

Sau pipeline hiện tại (ExtractBlueText → Dilate → UndoWaveDistortion → Resize → BitwiseNot), vẫn còn:
- Các chấm pixel lẻ tẻ nhỏ (isolated noise dots)
- Các đường kẻ mảnh còn sót từ wave distortion
- Các vùng nhiễu nhỏ không thuộc nét chữ số

## Giải pháp

Sau bước BitwiseNot (tạo ra forOcr), thêm 2 bước lọc:

### Bước 1: Thêm hàm RemoveSmallBlobs vào phần Image processing helpers

```csharp
/// Loại bỏ các blob nhỏ (nhiễu) bằng cách chỉ giữ lại các contour
/// có diện tích lớn hơn ngưỡng minAreaRatio * totalArea.
static Mat RemoveSmallBlobs(Mat blackOnWhite, double minAreaRatio = 0.003)
{
    using var inv = new Mat();
    Cv2.BitwiseNot(blackOnWhite, inv);

    Cv2.FindContours(inv, out var contours, out _,
        RetrievalModes.External, ContourApproximationModes.ApproxSimple);

    double totalArea = blackOnWhite.Width * blackOnWhite.Height;
    double minArea   = totalArea * minAreaRatio;

    var cleanMask = new Mat(blackOnWhite.Size(), MatType.CV_8UC1, new Scalar(255));
    for (int i = 0; i < contours.Length; i++)
    {
        if (Cv2.ContourArea(contours[i]) >= minArea)
            Cv2.DrawContours(cleanMask, contours, i, new Scalar(0), -1);
    }
    return cleanMask;
}
```

### Bước 2: Trong RecognizeCaptcha(), sau dòng Cv2.BitwiseNot(scaled, forOcr), thêm:

```csharp
// Loại pixel đơn lẻ bằng MedianBlur
using var medBlurred = new Mat();
Cv2.MedianBlur(forOcr, medBlurred, 3);

// Loại các blob nhỏ không phải nét số
using var cleaned = RemoveSmallBlobs(medBlurred, minAreaRatio: 0.003);
```

Sau đó dùng `cleaned` thay `forOcr` cho cả:
- TryFullImageOcr(cleaned)
- RecognizePerChar(cleaned, scaledW, scaledH)
- Lưu ảnh vào thư mục zzz

## Yêu cầu

1. Thêm hàm RemoveSmallBlobs() vào ConsoleApp1/Program.cs
2. Sửa RecognizeCaptcha() để áp dụng MedianBlur + RemoveSmallBlobs sau BitwiseNot
3. Dùng ảnh cleaned cho OCR và lưu vào zzz
4. Không thay đổi logic OCR (Tesseract, rotation, deskew)
5. Dispose() đúng chỗ cho tất cả Mat tạm


The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated):

User: trong chương trình có đoạn nào khử nhiễu ảnh chưa

Assistant: Chương trình **đã có xử lý khử nhiễu**, nhưng không dùng bộ lọc nhiễu truyền thống (như Gaussian Blur hay Median Filter). Thay vào đó, nhiễu được loại bỏ qua **pipeline tiền xử lý thông minh** gồm nhiều bước:

---

## Các bước khử nhiễu trong chương trình

### 1. 🎨 Lọc màu – `ExtractBlueText()` [`ConsoleApp1/Program.cs`](https://github.com/huynhvanduc/OCR/blob/658aef76da40e10becdd27dced4794f86b2c0c73/ConsoleApp1/Program.cs#L310-L351)
Đây là bước khử nhiễu **hiệu quả nhất** trong pipeline:
- Chỉ giữ lại các pixel **màu xanh lam đậm** (chữ số)
- Loại bỏ hoàn toàn **noise dots** (chấm nhiễu xám) và **đường nhiễu cong** — vì chúng có `R ≈ G ≈ B` (màu xám) → bị lọc ra
- Điều kiện: `B > 40 AND (B−R) > 18 AND (B−G) > 18`

### 2. 🔵 Morphological Close – trong `ExtractBlueText()`
```csharp
Cv2.MorphologyEx(mask, mask, MorphTypes.Close, kernel); // kernel Ellipse 3×3
```
Lấp các **lỗ hổng nhỏ** trong nét chữ do anti-aliasing tạo ra sau khi lọc màu.

### 3. 🔲 Dilate (giãn nở mask) – trong `RecognizeCaptcha()`
```csharp
Cv2.Dilate(blueMask, dilated, dilKernel); // kernel Ellipse 3×3
```
Điền thêm các pixel thiếu trong stroke, tăng độ liền mạch của nét chữ.

author: kackey621
body:
## Summary
Closes #20.

- `McpClient` required a manual `initialize()` handshake before any `tools/call`, but no Riverpod consumer was calling it. Concurrent UI-driven `callTool()` invocations could fire before init landed and could even duplicate the handshake.
- Adds an idempotent `Future<void>? _initFuture` latch: first caller starts the handshake, concurrent callers await the same `Future`, sequential callers short-circuit through the resolved `Future`. Failed init clears the latch so the next call retries.

## Changes
- `lib/data/datasources/remote/mcp/mcp_client.dart`: new private `_initFuture` field, `_ensureInitialized()` helper, `_doInitialize()` with fail-clear, `callTool()` awaits the latch first. `initialize()` kept as a public eager-init entry point that delegates to the latch.
- `test/unit/data/datasources/remote/mcp/mcp_client_test.dart`: 5 unit tests pinning concurrent-dedup, ordering, sequential reuse, explicit-init reuse, and failure-retry semantics.

## Verification
- [x] `flutter analyze` on the two touched files — *No issues found! (ran in 5.3s)*
- [x] `flutter test test/unit/data/datasources/remote/mcp/mcp_client_test.dart` — *All 5 tests passed*
- [x] `dart format` clean
- [x] `act -j analyze -n` dry-run valid (no workflow file touched)
- [N/A] Chrome smoke — MCP requires a running JSON-RPC backend; the latch behaviour is fully exercised by the unit tests.
- [x] Manual review: `_initFuture ??= _doInitialize()` is Dart-safe under the single-threaded event-loop model (no microtask preemption between the read and the write).

## Threat model
This is a correctness fix, not a security fix. Pre-fix consequences: spurious 500s when the MCP server rejected `tools/call` before `initialize`, and duplicate handshake load on the server. The fix is a pure client-side serialisation.

## Risk / out-of-band
- None. The change is additive and backward-compatible: existing callers that invoked `initialize()` explicitly continue to work (the latch is set on first call and reused thereafter).

La conception précédente avait une contradiction : un canal push "global" **et** des toggles par type. Désactiver tous les types ne désactivait pas le canal browser → la carte principale restait "ACTIVÉ" → confus pour l'utilisateur.

author: velissa-ai
body:
Followup to #30825.

## Problem

#30825 moved \`discardStreamingBuffer()\` and \`discardPartialOutputBuffer()\` into \`clearCurrentTurnTracking()\` to prevent stale flushes from creating orphan messages. But two callers in \`ChatActionHandler\` intentionally call \`flushPartialOutputBuffer()\` AFTER \`clearCurrentTurnTracking()\` to preserve tool-call output through cancel/error. With the new code, that flush became a no-op — accumulated tool output (e.g. partial bash stdout) was silently dropped.

## Fix

- \`handleGenerationCancelled\`: flush partial output BEFORE clearing turn tracking. Drop the now-redundant \`discardStreamingBuffer()\` (clearCurrentTurnTracking already discards it).
- \`handleConversationError\`: same — flush before clear.

## Secondary: thinking stale-ID symmetry

Devin also flagged asymmetry in \`ChatViewModel+StreamingHelpers\`: \`appendTextToCurrentMessage\` promotes buffered text to a new message on stale ID, but \`appendThinkingToCurrentMessage\` discarded thinking text. Since \`flushStreamingBuffer()\` calls \`flushThinkingBuffer()\` first, a stale flush could lose thinking content before the text flush salvaged itself. Made thinking symmetric — promote to a new message instead of discarding.

Addresses review comments from Codex and Devin on #30825.

author: alrobles
body:
## Summary

Adds a local-only bootstrap utility so operators on `reumanlab` or developer laptops can wire up the connector without ever sending the GitHub App private key through chat. The PEM body is never echoed to stdout, never logged, and never asked for as a string — only its **local path** is accepted.

- `scripts/bootstrap-github-app.sh` — interactive / flag-driven bootstrap
- `lib/env-writer.js` — pure helpers (parse, merge, atomic write @ mode 600, redact secrets, generate `CONNECTOR_TOKEN`)
- `scripts/env-writer-cli.js` — thin Node CLI wrapper for the bash script
- `test/env-writer.test.js` — 18 unit tests covering env writing, file mode, newline/NUL rejection, and token redaction
- `docs/bootstrap-github-app.md` — comparison of three flows: **manual local (recommended)**, encrypted handoff fallback, future App Manifest/OAuth wizard
- Runbook and `github-app-auth.md` get pointers so the manual `mkdir`/`chmod`/`cat > .env` steps are deprecated for the prototype path
- Wired into `npm test` as `test:env-writer`

## What the script does

Given `--app-id`, `--installation-id`, and `--key-path` (or interactive prompts), it:

1. Validates inputs (numeric IDs, PEM exists).
2. Runs `openssl pkey -noout` and prints only the **public-key SHA-256 fingerprint** so the operator can confirm the App identity without leaking the private key.
3. Copies the PEM into `~/.config/agenticplug/keys/github-app-private-key.pem` (`chmod 600` inside a `chmod 700` parent).
4. Generates a 32-byte random `CONNECTOR_TOKEN` if one isn't already present (idempotent — re-runs preserve the existing token).
5. Writes `~/.config/agenticplug/.env.connector` atomically with mode 600 and safe defaults: `CONNECTOR_HOST=127.0.0.1`, `GITHUB_ALLOWED_REPOS=alrobles/agenticplug` (overridable), `ALLOW_HPC_SUBMIT=false`.
6. Runs `systemctl --user daemon-reload` if a user session is present (best-effort, `--no-systemd` to skip).
7. Boots `connector/main.js` on a random high port for ~3 s to confirm the fail-closed startup checks pass, then stops it (`--no-startup-check` to skip).

`--dry-run` is supported for review of all destination paths before any write happens. The script does not modify any system unit file, never touches `/opt`, and never binds a public port.

## Why this is safe

- The script never asks for the PEM body — only its path. Operators move the file in/out of the host via their own trusted channel (browser download or `scp`).
- Env-file writes are atomic (temp file + fsync + rename), and `chmod 600` is applied **before** rename so there is no readable window.
- Values containing newlines or NUL bytes are refused (`validateValue`) — defense against env-file injection through interpolated args.
- The summary printed by the script after writing the env file uses `redactValue` for any key matching `TOKEN|SECRET|PRIVATE_KEY|PAT|PASSWORD|API_KEY` — token-shaped values display as `xx…yy (N chars)` so operators can sanity-check without leaking.
- The startup probe binds a random high port on `127.0.0.1` and is killed within 3 s.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — proxy (10), connector (15), github-app-auth, github-runtime, hpc (53), connector-doctor (4), env-writer (18) all pass locally.
- [x] Manual smoke test with a throwaway 2048-bit RSA PEM:
  - Fresh run creates env file (mode 600) and keys dir (mode 700) with PEM at mode 600.
  - Re-run with different App ID preserves the existing `CONNECTOR_TOKEN`.
  - `--dry-run` performs no filesystem writes.
  - Startup probe successfully boots the real `connector/main.js`, sees the "listening" marker, and stops it.
- [ ] Reviewer to manually verify on `reumanlab` that the flow works end-to-end with a **real** App PEM (not part of this PR; deliberately out of scope to avoid touching live deployment).

## Out of scope

- No changes to `connector/main.js` or any runtime path.
- No changes to systemd unit templates or `/opt/agenticplug` paths.
- No public tunnel; the script never binds outside `127.0.0.1`.
- Future App Manifest/OAuth wizard is described in `docs/bootstrap-github-app.md` but not implemented here.

## Summary

e2e-coder Scenario G dogfood (2026-05-17) probed `reyn chat` capability questions ("what can you do?" / 「何ができる?」) on a fresh-install workspace. The weak default model (`gemini-2.5-flash-lite`) echoes router-internal vocabulary in JA reply text — `invoke_action`, `list_actions`, `skill__X`, `file__X`, etc. EN replies are mostly clean because the base model's English chat prior suppresses the leak; JA lacks an equivalent prior.

This PR is **documentation only** — no SP / code change. The decision is "do not adopt a prompt-level workaround", surfaced via the README weak-model warning + a new giveup-tracker entry **G31**.

## Trace-driven analysis

`scripts/dogfood_trace.py --mode llm-tools-schema` confirmed the leak source: tool descriptions themselves reference `invoke_action` 27 times because the LLM needs the name to call the function-calling API. The leak is load-bearing-name reproduction, not a router bug. Structural cleanse (= PR #105 for `skill__code_review` hallucination) handles example-name fabrication but cannot eliminate load-bearing names.

`scripts/llm_replay.py --patch` was used to A/B candidate SP rules against the same captured trace (= no fixture re-record, no production change):

| Model | SP rule | text-reply clean rate (N=10) |
|---|---|---|
| flash-lite (weak default) | none | 20% |
| flash-lite | Variant A (specific examples + multilingual) | 60% |
| flash-lite | Variant B (generic abstract) | 10% |
| flash-lite | Variant C (minimal 1-sentence) | 0% |
| **flash (strong)** | none | **87.5%** |
| flash (strong) | Variant A | 100% |
| flash + thinking_budget=4000 | none | 60% |
| flash + thinking_budget=4000 | Variant A | 100% |

## Decision

**Policy-accepted: do not adopt the SP rule.**

- Variant A closes 50-75% of the gap on weak, but is shaped as a prompt-level workaround (= enumerates specific phrasings + function names + multilingual examples). Generic / minimal variants are empirically ineffective at the weak tier.
- Strong model is **already** 87.5% clean with no prompt change — the gap is a known weak-model capability ceiling, not a Reyn design defect.
- Adopting Variant A violates the Reyn thesis ("weak models to be reliable through structural constraints, NOT prompt-level workarounds", README's "How Reyn compares" section).
- The cost ladder is exposed via the existing README note: cost-sensitive users keep weak + accept the leak; reply-quality-sensitive users edit `models.standard` and get near-zero leak.

- `README.md` — the existing "A note on weak default models" callout now lists both known weak-tier rough edges (G12 empty-replies + G31 capability-question leak) with N=10 numbers and a single pointer to the tracker.

## Problem

Akash providers run host-strict nginx-ingress, configured only for the auto-generated provider-issued hostname. When Cloudflare proxies `functions-api.akash.network` through to the origin, the request lands at the provider's ingress with `Host: functions-api.akash.network` — which has no matching rule, so nginx-ingress returns its default-backend 404.

Verified during prod bootstrap: curling the origin directly returns `{"ok":true,...}`; curling the same origin with `Host: functions-api.akash.network` returns nginx's `404 Not Found`. Same 404 reaches the browser through Cloudflare.

## Fix

Add an `accept` block to each service's `expose` entry. The provider reads it at deploy/rebind time and configures nginx-ingress to also route the listed hostnames to the pod. No Cloudflare Origin Rules, no Workers, no host-header manipulation needed.

- [deploy/server.sdl.yaml](deploy/server.sdl.yaml): `accept: [functions-api.akash.network]`
- [deploy/web.sdl.yaml](deploy/web.sdl.yaml): `accept: [functions.akash.network]`

## What happens on merge

CI rebinds both leases on the existing dseqs with the new SDLs. The provider reconfigures its ingress within ~30s. Then `curl https://functions-api.akash.network/api/health` works without any further Cloudflare-side config.

## Caveat

Not every Akash provider honors `accept` — some restrict their ingress to the auto-generated hostname. The provider used here is audited and is expected to support it. If we see continued 404s after the rebind, fallback is a Cloudflare Origin Rule (host rewrite) on the user side.

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge → CI rebinds both leases with new SDLs → provider reconfigures ingress.
- [ ] `curl https://functions-api.akash.network/api/health` returns `{"ok":true,...}`.
- [ ] `curl https://functions.akash.network/` returns the SPA HTML (after the second DNS record is in).

body:
### Motivation
- Improve fidelity of the Snooker Champion playfield so ball behavior matches physical cushions, jaws and pocket mouths. 
- Make ball rolling, spin transfer and strike power feel natural on the full-size snooker playfield. 
- Prevent the human avatar from stepping onto the playfield and align player-perspective camera to the chest for an authentic cue-side view. 
- Reduce visible artifacts (unnatural sideways drift, incorrect pocket captures) by modelling pocket mouths and jaw collisions. 

### Description
- Reworked playfield/pocket mapping into a measured pocket map and metadata (`createSnookerPocketMap`) including visual radii, mouth widths and jaw collider points and replaced the previous hardcoded pocket array. 
- Tuned physics constants: lowered ball visual lift, adjusted `SNOOKER_SHOT_POWER_BOOST`, spin scales, rolling resistance, friction, stop thresholds and spin damping to produce more realistic speed, spin and stopping behavior. 
- Added pocket-throat and jaw collision logic and integrated `applySnookerJawCollision` into `updateBalls`, so near-mouth misses collide with jaws/cushions instead of sliding through. 
- Reworked cue-strike launch (velocity/omega/spin transfer) and simplified spin controller to rely on angular velocity for realistic side/screw effects, and adjusted bridge/hand offsets, human scale and walkway projection so the avatar stays outside the table and the left hand sits more inward under the cue. 
- Blended cue-follow camera toward the player chest by passing live `human.chestWorld` into `resolveSnookerCueCameraPose` and using it to lerp the cue-follow camera for a player-perspective shot view. 

### Testing
- Built production bundle with `npm --prefix webapp run build` and the Vite build completed successfully. 
- Installed Playwright and system deps with `npx --yes playwright install chromium` and `npx --yes playwright install-deps chromium` which completed successfully. 
- Launched the dev server and ran a Playwright smoke test that opened `/games/snookerchampion` and saved a screenshot to `/tmp/snooker-champion-screenshot.png`, and the automated smoke test completed with no page errors.

author: unobtainiumrock
body:
## What

Continues the `worktree-server` → `worktree-bg` extraction started in PR #4. This PR relocates 4 local-daemon module trees (watcher, engine, sync, service) into `worktree-bg`, plus splits `config/settings.rs` so each runtime owns its own config types. **5 commits, conservative scope.**

Commits in order:

1. `bf7995a` — `feat(bg): define BgError enum` (pre-declares all variants subsequent commits use)
2. `9b8d83c` — `feat(bg): split config — move WatcherConfig + AutoSnapshotConfig to bg`
3. `e14ae67` — `feat(bg): move watcher + engine modules from worktree-server` (combined: `engine/event.rs` imports `watcher::debounce::DebouncedEvent`)
4. `7d89432` — `feat(bg): move sync module from worktree-server`
5. `b96f5f4` — `feat(bg): move service module from worktree-server` (also renames `service_name()` from `"worktree-server"` → `"worktree-bg"` for desktop daemon naming correctness; adds `BgError::Config` variant for `install.rs`)

## Why

`Server.md §23 step 1` and `BgProcess.md §22 Phase 1` both call for extracting local-daemon code from the misnamed `worktree-server` crate. PR #4 created the empty `worktree-bg` skeleton; this PR moves the actually-bg-side modules into it.

Each move has a direct spec citation:

| Move | Spec citation |
|---|---|
| watcher → bg | BgProcess.md §3: "Filesystem Watcher subsystem — OS-native event monitoring" |
| engine → bg | BgProcess.md §3 + §6 (whole "Auto-Snapshot Engine" section); Server.md §2 explicit non-responsibility: "Never creates auto-snapshots — it only stores what the bgprocess sends" |
| sync → bg | Sync.md: sync is "between the bgprocess (local) and the W0rkTree server (remote)" — push/pull/transport are the bg-side CLIENT |
| service → bg | BgProcess.md §2: "A platform-native service managed by the OS service manager" listed under What the bgprocess IS. Server.md §19 has its own separate cloud-native server lifecycle |

No spec interpretation required — each move points at explicit spec text.

## How

**Conservative scope by design.** The original plan was 10 commits with several spec-interpretation calls; user review flagged 4 of those as overreaches. This re-plan ships only the moves that are unambiguously safe:

- ✅ **Whole-module moves only** — no internal refactors
- ✅ **Per-commit `cargo check --workspace` green** — bisectable
- ✅ **`lib.rs` ordering preserved character-for-character** minus removed lines (no alphabetical reordering or other churn)
- ✅ **No orphan removals** — ServerError variants and `notify` dep that become unused stay in place; cleanup is deferred
- ✅ **`ServerError` → `BgError` substitutions only where the moved code references error variants**

What's explicitly **NOT in this PR** (deferred to follow-up tickets — see "Follow-up work" below):
- `worktree-server/src/git/` move — spec is ambiguous about whether server has Git interop, needs deeper read
- `auth/session.rs` split (session → bg, enforcer stays) — needs careful read of both files
- Storage extraction to protocol — wait until bg actually needs `StorageBackend`
- `api/handlers.rs` re-verification — snapshot/branch handlers might be CLI↔bg IPC per BgProcess.md §14
- `ServerError` variant cleanup — needs exhaustive workspace-wide grep first
- `worktree-server/Cargo.toml` dep prune — cosmetic, deferred

## Spec Reference

- `crates/worktree-protocol/specs/bgprocess/BgProcess.md` — §2 What the bgprocess IS, §3 Architecture, §6 Auto-Snapshot Engine, §14 CLI Communication (IPC), §22 Migration Plan
- `crates/worktree-protocol/specs/server/Server.md` — §2 What the Server Is NOT, §19 Server Lifecycle, §23 Implementation Status (step 1)
- `crates/worktree-protocol/specs/sync/Sync.md` — Sync as bg↔server protocol
- `crates/worktree-protocol/specs/README.md` — Two-Runtime architecture
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — Project Philosophy principle 2 ("Snapshot, not commit") — referenced for the auto_commit→auto_snapshot follow-up below

## Testing

- `cargo check --workspace` green after every commit (5 bisectable checkpoints — verified locally).
- `cargo build -p worktree-bg` produces binary that prints `worktree-bg: not yet implemented (skeleton — WT-EXTRACT-1)` (main.rs from PR #4 unchanged).
- `cargo build -p worktree-server` builds — slimmed crate now compiles with just `config/`, `git/`, `storage/`, `auth/`, `api/`, `error.rs`, `lib.rs`, `main.rs`.
- `cargo test -p worktree-bg` → **6 tests pass, 0 fail** (3 in `watcher/debounce.rs`, 3 in `sync/transport.rs` — all inline tests that traveled with their files).
- `grep -rn 'use worktree_server' crates/worktree-bg/` → zero hits (bg doesn't depend on server).
- `grep -rn 'use worktree_bg' crates/worktree-server/` → zero hits (server doesn't depend on bg — direction we want for the eventual Go rewrite).

Git history shows the deletes as renames (auto-detected from ≥50% content similarity), so `git log --follow` on any moved file shows full history.

## Follow-up work (will be filed as PF tasks)

This PR deliberately leaves headroom for these in separate tickets:

- **WT-EXTRACT-2b** — 6 deferred items (git/ move investigation, auth split, storage extraction, api/handlers re-verification, ServerError variant cleanup, Cargo.toml dep prune)
- **WT-RENAME-1** — Rename `auto_commit.rs` → `auto_snapshot.rs` and `AutoCommitEngine` → `AutoSnapshotEngine` to align with CONTRIBUTING.md principle 2 ("Snapshot, not commit") and BgProcess.md §6's spec section name "Auto-Snapshot Engine". This file's name was inconsistent before WT-EXTRACT-2; just moving it preserves the misnomer.
- **WT-DOCS-2** — Add unified bg↔server sync sequence + state-machine Mermaid diagrams to Sync.md (current spec has ASCII per-flow diagrams but no unified picture).
- **WT-DOCS-3** — Document sync failure modes (server-unreachable mid-push, conflict-on-stale-tip, retry semantics).

## Pre-existing workspace state (transparent disclosure)

Same disclosure pattern as PR #4. CONTRIBUTING.md's checklist requires `bash scripts/ci.sh` to pass. Three pre-existing issues unrelated to this PR remain on upstream main:

1. **~93 fmt violations + 21+ clippy errors** across `worktree-protocol`, `worktree-cli`, `worktree-sdk`, `worktree-git`, and the un-moved parts of `worktree-server` (filed as `WT-CI-1` in our internal tracker).
2. **`cargo test -p worktree-server` fails with 3 errors in `auth/enforcer.rs`** — `Scope::Tree(TenantId, TreeId)` enum variant expects 2 args, tests pass 1. This file is **not in this PR's diff** (verified via `git diff upstream/main..HEAD --stat`); it's pre-existing breakage that may have been masked by missing CI runs. I can author a follow-up fix PR if desired.
3. **`ServerError::Watcher`, `ServerError::Engine` variants now unused** after the moves in this PR. Kept in place per the "no orphan removals" rule; cleanup is queued as WT-EXTRACT-2b item 5.

My files pass scoped checks: `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` on the worktree-bg crate are clean.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added/updated — inline tests traveled with moved files; cargo test -p worktree-bg passes 6/6
- [x] Documentation updated — N/A for module relocations (spec docs already describe the eventual architecture; this PR brings code into alignment with them)
- [x] Spec updated — N/A
- [ ] `bash scripts/ci.sh` passes locally — **fails on pre-existing workspace fmt/clippy debt and pre-existing `auth/enforcer.rs` test breakage**, neither of which is introduced by this PR. Scoped checks against my own files pass.
